pr_title: delete dead branches in process visitor to reduce dead dependencies
pr_comments:
> Link [Height](https://parcel.height.app) tasks by mentioning a task ID in the pull request title or description, commit messages, or comments.
>
> You can also use "Close T-X" to automatically close a task when the pull request is merged.

> But why is the test failing? Did I miss something? Do we need to have another approach? And is this an issue at all? Maybe you have some ideas on that :)

Yeah, it's actually a bit more complicated:

- remove dead branches completely so that the imported binding referenced at all (your current changes)
- In the `hoist.js` visitor, only add import declarations that are actually referenced to `dep.symbols` (the reason for the previous step is that this is now a very cheap operation).
The non-scope-hoisting `dependencies.js` visitor has no symbol handling at all, so doing this for `--no-scope-hoist` and watch mode would be a bit more work.
- the transformer doesn't know if a dependency has `sideEffects: false`, so in `@parcel/core` we can exclude side-effect-free dependencies that have no used symbols (similar to https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/f88eb6822d76002c9c900ab7ec50154f8490688f/packages/core/core/src/requests/DepPathRequestRunner.js#L63) - it might also work out of the box with the current `deferring` mechanism

I think this should be handled in the Rust rewrite. We use SWC's branch optimizer which should completely remove dead branches, and this is run prior to dependency collection and process/global insertion.

issue_context.title: Dead Code of Dependencies not removed
comments:
> For the latter example, I am actually not sure if it is a bug, as the react-dom does not have sideeffects: false set in package.json.

That would be the first step. But at the moment `index.js` would still have "act" marked as imported in `asset.symbols`, so it would still be included. 
Two ways to fix this:
1.  In `hoist.js` for `ImportDeclaration`, don't add it if: for every reference to the imported symbol there is a falsy conditional-statement among the node's ancestors (this sounds very expensive).
2. in the `JSTransformer` visitors  that does the `process.env` inlining, directly remove the unused branch from the AST (I think this is the better solution)

> But inserting the Buffer in the first example is unexpected.

Will open a PR for that in a bit.

> Will open a PR for that in a bit.

That was fast, really cool 😃  I can prove it's working!

> in the JSTransformer visitors that does the process.env inlining, directly remove the unused branch from the AST (I think this is the better solution)

I gave it a try, but have some questions about it. Maybe you like to have a look? (see the linked PR) :)

Your case doesn't have to do anything with this issue, but `process.env.NODE_ENV` is replaced by Parcel itself by `"development"` or `"production"` and then afterwards Terser would remove that whole if statement.

You're in the right issue after all, but that wasn't really obvious from your first example 😬 . And that's the workaround that I would have suggested as well.

(With scope-hoisting, the first case should work because the json should get removed. If not, that's easier to fix that this issue itself).
